description: A group of space enthusiasts with love for our planet and beyond
summary: Echoes is an immersive and interactive educational platform that brings the stories of NASA's abandoned and retired space equipment back to life. Through 3D exploration, interactive models, and visual storytelling, visitors can discover the spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments that helped us explore the Moon and Mars. Rather than simply presenting historical facts, Echoes invites users to explore these machines, uncover the stories behind their missions, understand the discoveries, and learn why they were eventually left behind. By combining interactive models, mission timelines, NASA imagery, and accessible scientific explanations, we transform complex space exploration history into an engaging experience for school-age audiences. Echoes is built based on one simple idea: a mission may end, but its legacy continues. Every piece of abandoned equipment represents human ingenuity, scientific progress, and lessons that shape future exploration. Through Echoes, we hope to preserve these stories and inspire the next generation of space enthusiasts.
details:
Echoes

What our project does and how It works

Echoes is an interactive, web based educational platform that tells the stories of NASA's abandoned and retired equipment on the Moon and Mars. Instead of focusing exclusively on launches, achievements, and discoveries, our project explores what happens to spacecraft after their missions end and why their contributions remain important. The platform combines interactive 3D environments, spacecraft models, mission timelines, NASA imagery, and scientific storytelling to create an engaging experience for school-age audiences. Visitors can explore space environments, interact with individual pieces of equipment, and discover their histories through visually organized information. Each featured object introduces its original purpose, operational history, major scientific discoveries, and the circumstances surrounding the end of its mission. These stories also demonstrate how knowledge gained from earlier missions continues to influence modern space exploration. Our goal is to make visitors feel as though they are discovering these machines themselves rather than simply reading about them.

Development and technology

We developed Echoes using Claude Code, an AI coding tool that supported the implementation, refinement, and troubleshooting of our interactive website.

Our development process focused on integrating several components into a cohesive educational experience:

  • Interactive 3D visualization: Allowing visitors to explore spacecraft and space environments through engaging visual interactions.
  • NASA scientific resources: Incorporating publicly available mission documentation, historical records, and imagery to support accurate educational content.
  • Visual storytelling: Combining mission timelines, scientific explanations, historical photographs, and interactive elements.
  • Responsive interface design: Creating an accessible experience across different screen sizes.
  • Performance optimization: Refining the loading, rendering, and presentation of images and interactive elements to improve usability.

Using Claude Code allowed us to develop and refine the website's functionality and presentation while maintaining control over its overall direction, educational content, and user experience.

Creativity and innovation

The central idea behind Echoes is that a mission may end, but its legacy continues. NASA's retired equipment is often documented through technical reports, archival photographs, and individual mission websites. Although these resources provide valuable information, younger audiences may find them difficult to explore or connect with. Echoes transforms these scattered stories into a unified, interactive experience. Rather than presenting abandoned spacecraft as forgotten machinery, we highlight the scientific discoveries, engineering challenges, and human decisions behind each mission. We wanted to move beyond the conventional educational website. Instead of relying on long paragraphs and static pages, Echoes emphasizes interactive discovery, immersive environments, and visual storytelling. Visitors can follow their curiosity, investigate individual missions, and discover connections between historical achievements and future space exploration.

Design considerations and challenges

Throughout development, our team considered four major priorities: scientific accuracy, accessibility, visual engagement, and technical performance. One challenge was presenting complex scientific information in a way that school-age audiences could understand without sacrificing accuracy. We addressed this by organizing information into concise explanations supported by visuals and additional context. Another consideration was ensuring that the website remained engaging without overwhelming. We focused on intuitive navigation, consistent design, readable layouts, and interactive elements that serve an educational purpose. We also worked on improving image loading, 3D presentation, website responsiveness, and consistency between different sections to make the experience as smooth and accessible as possible.

Intended impact and benefits

Echoes aims to make NASA's exploration history more accessible, engaging, and memorable for students and space enthusiasts. Through interactive exploration, visitors can learn about spacecraft engineering, planetary science, scientific instrumentation, and the challenges of operating equipment in extreme environments. Beyond communicating historical facts, our project encourages curiosity and critical thinking. What was each machine designed to accomplish? What challenges did it encounter? What discoveries did it make possible? How did those discoveries influence subsequent missions? We believe these questions help students understand that scientific progress is not defined solely by successful missions. Unexpected failures, technical limitations, and retired equipment can all contribute valuable knowledge to future exploration. Ultimately, Echoes seeks to preserve the stories of these remarkable machines while inspiring the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers.
